text: Setting clear goals is the foundation of any successful project. A useful approach is to create SMART goals, which means they are Specific, Measurable, Achievable, Relevant, and Time-bound. Instead of saying "improve the website," a SMART goal would be "increase page load speed by 20% within three months." Once the main goal is set, you should break the work into smaller milestones—these are checkpoints that show progress and keep the team motivated. Each milestone should have a clear deliverable, such as a final report or a working prototype. Finally, ensure stakeholder alignment by regularly communicating with everyone involved. This confirms that the project's direction meets their expectations and prevents misunderstandings later on.
